findings: [major] Live API secret hardcoded at billing/reconcile.py:1 — PARTNER_API_KEY = "sk-live-..." is a production credential now permanently in git history. Requires key rotation (deletion does not un-leak it) plus env/secret-manager lookup at call time; it is also a module-level global and therefore importable elsewhere.

[major] Off-by-one at billing/reconcile.py:7 — loop bound changed from range(0, len(rows)) to range(1, len(rows)), silently excluding rows[0].amount from every reconciliation. Correct ledgers report mismatched, and a ledger short by exactly rows[0] reports as balanced. Unmotivated by the rest of the diff and contradicted by the unchanged docstring.

[major] billing/reconcile.py:14 calls http_client.get(...) but no such name is defined or imported anywhere in the change set; if unbound, every call raises NameError at call time (not import time), so an import-only smoke test misses it. Stated as unresolved-within-diff: verify against the full file, since the hunk headers are unreliable.

[major] billing/reconcile.py:12-18 — new public fetch_partner_balance with URL construction, auth header assembly, and JSON parsing ships with no tests. Locking assertion: with a stub whose .json() yields {"balance": 42.0}, fetch_partner_balance("p1") returns 42.0 and requests .../partners/p1/balance; that test cannot pass on today's code, so it also settles the http_client question.

[minor] billing/test_reconcile.py:9-11 — the added test_reconcile_rejects_mismatched_total is always-green: rows sum to 60.0 correct and 50.0 buggy, both far from expected_total=999.0. Locking assertion needed instead: reconcile_ledger_rows([10.0,20.0,30.0], expected_total=50.0) must be False — it returns True today because the skipped first row makes the buggy total exactly 50.0.

[minor] billing/reconcile.py:15 — unvalidated partner_id interpolated into an internal URL path; a value containing ../, ?, or # reaches a different endpoint on a trusting internal service. Escalates to [major] if partner_id originates from request input, which the diff does not show.

[minor] billing/reconcile.py:12-18 — HTTP I/O placed in a previously dependency-free pure-computation module; belongs in the billing API-client module alongside shared client/auth/retry setup, and its presence here drags a network dependency into every importer of the reconciler.

[minor] billing/reconcile.py:14-18 — no timeout (hung upstream hangs the caller), no status check (4xx/5xx bodies parsed as success, so auth failures surface as KeyError far from the cause), and no guard on response.json()["balance"]. The value feeds money reconciliation, where a silently wrong result is worse than a loud failure.

[minor] billing/reconcile.py:6-8 — manual index loop reimplements the sum() built-in; sum(row.amount for row in rows) has no bound to get wrong, and the index arithmetic is precisely what made the off-by-one expressible. In scope because range(0 -> range(1 genuinely changed.

[minor] billing/reconcile.py:6,9 — float accumulation and a magic 0.01 tolerance for monetary values; error grows with row count while the fixed tolerance does not. Decimal plus a named constant is the fix. Scope caveat: these lines are behaviorally unchanged, so this belongs in a Remaining section rather than blocking.
[nitpick] billing/reconcile.py:5 — docstring does not state that the comparison is approximate, what the tolerance is, or that the return is a bool, despite the 0.01 being load-bearing.

[nitpick] billing/test_reconcile.py:10 — the new test uses Row(...) with no import; likely supplied by a conftest.py, matching the pre-existing test's pattern, so graded low. If no conftest.py exists, both tests error on collection and this is [major].

[nitpick] billing/test_reconcile.py:5,10 — the three-row fixture literal is duplicated across both tests; a shared fixture or parametrize over (expected_total, want) would carry the missing boundary case without a third copy.
